# United States Property Market Profile

## Structural Characteristics
- Population: ~340M | Housing stock: ~145M units
- Homeownership rate: ~66%
- 30-year fixed-rate mortgage = dominant product (~90% of new loans, government-guaranteed via Fannie/Freddie/FHA)
- Key institutions: FHFA, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, FHA, Case-Shiller (S&P), NAR, Census Bureau

## The 30-Year Fixed Mortgage — US Structural Advantage

The 30-year fixed-rate, pre-payable mortgage is uniquely American:
- Government guarantee (GSEs) makes 30Y fixed possible at reasonable rates
- Borrowers can refinance when rates fall — but are insulated when rates rise
- This creates a "lock-in effect": homeowners with 3% mortgages won't sell when rates are 7%
- Result: Existing home sales freeze during rate hiking cycles, but forced selling is minimal
- This makes US housing corrections fundamentally different from AU/NZ/UK (where adjustable rates force rapid adjustment)

## Historical Cycle Phases

| Period | Phase | Key Driver |
|--------|-------|------------|
| 1997-2006 | Boom (+80% real) | Subprime, securitization, low rates, speculation |
| 2007-2012 | Bust (-35% real national, -50%+ in bubble markets) | GFC, foreclosure crisis |
| 2012-2019 | Recovery (+50%) | Post-GFC normalization, supply shortage |
| 2020-2022 | Boom (+40%) | Pandemic: WFH, low rates, fiscal stimulus, supply crunch |
| 2022-2023 | Correction (-5% nominal, flat real) | Mortgage rates from 3% → 7.5% |
| 2023-2025 | Divergence: nominal up, real flat | Lock-in effect suppressing supply |

## Key US-Specific Drivers

### 1. The Lock-In Effect
- 90%+ of outstanding mortgages have rates below 5%
- 60%+ have rates below 4%
- Selling means trading a 3% mortgage for a 7% mortgage → extreme disincentive
- Result: Existing home sales at 30-year lows, inventory near historic lows
- Homebuilders (new construction) benefiting disproportionately — they have no lock-in

### 2. Regional Divergence
| Region | Characteristic | Current Cycle |
|--------|---------------|---------------|
| Sun Belt (TX, FL, AZ, NC, TN) | High in-migration, pro-building | Strong — supply responsive |
| West Coast (CA, WA, OR) | Severe supply constraints, high prices | Correction then recovery |
| Northeast (NY, NJ, MA) | High prices, low migration, constrained | Flat to moderate |
| Midwest (OH, MI, IN, IL) | Affordable, slow growth | Stable |
| Mountain West (CO, UT, ID) | Pandemic boom markets | Sharp correction then recovery |

### 3. Housing Supply
- Structural deficit estimated at 3-6M units (underbuilding since GFC)
- Zoning restrictions (single-family zoning, minimum lot sizes, parking requirements)
- Labor shortage in construction trades
- Lumber and materials costs volatile

### 4. Institutional Investors
- Single-family rental (SFR) REITs: Invitation Homes, American Homes 4 Rent, Progress Residential
- Institutional ownership ~3-5% of single-family homes nationally, much higher in Sun Belt
- Build-to-rent (BTR) = growing trend — entire subdivisions built for rental
- Wall Street buying peaked 2021-2022, slowed significantly as rates rose

## Affordability Benchmarks

| Metric | Los Angeles | New York | Dallas | National |
|--------|-----------|----------|--------|----------|
| Median Price | $900K-$1.1M | $650-750K | $350-400K | $400-450K |
| Price-to-Income | ~10-12x | ~7-9x | ~4-5x | ~5-6x |
| Price-to-Rent | ~25-30x | ~22-27x | ~12-15x | ~16-20x |
| Mortgage % of Income* | 50-60% | 40-50% | 25-30% | 30-35% |

*At 7% rate, 30Y fixed, 20% down

## Key Risks

### Downside
- Rates sustained at 7%+ = affordability crisis deepens, transaction volume paralyzed
- Commercial real estate (office) crisis spilling to multifamily
- Insurance crisis (FL, CA — insurers exiting, premiums unaffordable)
- Regional bank exposure to CRE loans (especially smaller banks)

### Upside
- Rate cuts → refi wave → unlock existing home inventory → normalize market
- Millennial/Gen Z household formation = structural demand tailwind
- Homebuilder consolidation → better margins, disciplined supply
- Immigration (legal + unauthorized) = population growth supports demand

### Cycle Assessment
- Phase: Correction in volume, not price (unique to US due to lock-in effect)
- National nominal prices near ATH, real prices flat to slightly down
- Most resilient major housing market globally due to 30Y fixed structure
- Key risk: If unemployment rises significantly, the lock-in effect disappears (forced sellers)
